inventory.title: Relational comparison and boolean contexts
items: Relational comparison of BigInts and Numbers

scopeExclusions: Parsing strings into numeric values with Number and BigInt methods
Arithmetic operator behavior beyond conversion and comparison
accuracyFacts: ECMAScript 2026 defines ToInt8, ToUint8, ToInt16, ToUint16, ToInt32, and ToUint32 as Number conversions that truncate toward zero and wrap modulo the relevant bit width; signed forms reinterpret the high bit as negative. Non-finite and zero values become positive zero.
ToUint8Clamp clamps to 0–255 and rounds ties to even; NaN becomes positive zero. It does not wrap.

ToBigInt accepts Boolean, BigInt, and grammar-valid String primitives (after object-to-primitive conversion); it rejects Number, Symbol, null, and undefined. ToBigInt64 and ToBigUint64 wrap modulo 2^64 and return signed/unsigned 64-bit-range BigInts.
Abstract ToString(Symbol()) throws TypeError, but the explicit String(Symbol()) function has a special case and succeeds.
ToNumber rejects BigInt and Symbol; Number() has an explicit BigInt case that can lose precision; unary plus follows ToNumber and rejects BigInt.
For mixed BigInt/Number loose equality, both values must be finite and have equal exact mathematical values; BigInt does not equal NaN or either infinity.
The legacy [[IsHTMLDDA]] loose-equality exception is operand-sensitive: document.all == null is true while null == document.all is false; document.all remains a browser-host compatibility exception.
String relational comparison is lexicographic by UTF-16 code units, not code points, locale collation, or Unicode-normalized equivalence.
